title: SB0939 (112th General Assembly): AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 36 and Title 39, relative to emergency protection orders.

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, Tennessee); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Tennessee text (Draft, 2021-02-10; crossfiled twin's official copy via the Internet Archive snapshot 20260514163034 of https://www.capitol.tn.gov/Bills/112/Bill/HB1292.pdf (it names SENATE BILL 939; own link https://www.capitol.tn.gov/Bills/112/Bill/SB0939.pdf not archived))

operative_text:
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1901): (a) Any family member, household member, intimate partner, or law enforcement officer who has a reasonable belief that a person poses an imminent risk of harm to the person or others if allowed to purchase or possess a firearm may seek relief under this section by filing a sworn petition for an emergency protection order against the respondent.
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1902): An ex parte emergency protection order prohibits the respondent from purchasing or possessing any firearm during the period that the order is in effect.
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1902(b)): If no ex parte emergency protection order has been issued as of the time of the hearing, and the petitioner has proven the allegation of an imminent risk of harm by a preponderance of the evidence, the court may, at that time, issue an emergency protection order prohibiting the respondent from purchasing or possessing any firearm for a definite period of time, not to exceed one (1) year.
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1905(b)(1)): To terminate the respondent's physical possession of the firearms in the respondent's possession by any lawful means, such as transferring possession to a third party who is not prohibited from possessing firearms, within forty-eight (48) hours; and
SECTION 1 (new TCA 39-17-1905(f)(2)): A violation of subdivision (f)(1) is a Class A misdemeanor and each violation constitutes a separate offense.
